The hearers' received faith becomes an example during continued suffering

Verse 5 says the readers saw what kind of men the writers were. Verse 6 says the readers then became imitators of them and of the Lord. The likeness is specific. They received the word in much affliction. They also received it with joy from the Holy Spirit. Trouble and joy together is the pattern they copied. Verse 7 shows it passing on: they became an example to other believers.
Remembered care supports trust while painful separation remains unresolved

Verses 3–6 deny wrong motives: deceit, flattery, greed, and a search for glory. Verse 7 gives the opposite picture: a nursing mother. Verse 8 says what that care amounted to. They gave the good news, and they gave their own souls. The reason is affection: the readers had become very dear to them. Verse 9 offers proof the readers can remember: labor night and day.
Timothy's report turns fear about separation into comfort and renewed prayer

Verse 5 states Paul’s fear: the tempter may have undone the work. He sent Timothy because he could bear it no longer. Verse 6 reports the answer, and it has three parts. Their faith holds, their love holds, and they remember the writers kindly. The third part matters to a man torn away from them (2:17). They long to see him as he longs to see them. Verse 7 says this comforted him in his own distress.
Careful conduct and hope for the dead answer different forms of harm and fear

Verse 13 gives the purpose of the passage. Paul does not want them to grieve like those who have no hope. The worry seems to be that the dead will miss the Lord’s coming. Verse 15 answers it: the living will not go ahead of the dead. Verse 16 puts the dead in Christ first. Verse 17 ends with all of them together with the Lord. Verse 18 tells them to use these words to comfort each other.
An unknown day calls for alert care rather than a calculated schedule

Verses 12–13 speak of those who lead. Verse 14 then gives a task to the “brothers,” the whole group. It names three kinds of people and three different responses. The disorderly are admonished, the faint-hearted encouraged, and the weak supported. One response covers everyone: patience. Verse 15 adds the limit: no one may repay evil for evil.
